title: The calibration battery's cell table: which specimen is read by which extractor, through which symbol list, against which co-resident control
readMeFirst: This file is the STANDARD's table. It says what is measured. It deliberately does NOT say what the answer should be -- that is claims/expected.json, and the two are separate files so that the thing which PRODUCES a reading never opens the file holding the answers. scripts/run-battery.sh reads this one and never that one; scripts/check-battery.py reads both.

standardRevision is an integer and generatorSha256 is the sha-256 of tools/make-battery.sh. A generator that changed is a different standard: run-battery.sh recomputes the digest at measurement time and refuses to measure when it has moved without this file moving with it. Without that pin the battery would silently become a different battery between two runs whose reports look comparable.

The `role` column separates the two kinds of cell, and mixing them is how a battery stops meaning anything. A `reference` cell has a known true value and the extractor is expected to read it: a disagreement is a defect in the extractor. An `instrument-limit-probe` cell has a known true value the extractor is expected to MISREAD, and the misreading is documented prose in compiler/schema/properties.json: a disagreement there is a defect in the prose or in the extractor, and which one it is has to be worked out rather than assumed.

wipe.polarity: a non-zero count is the property being enforced
wipe.symbolsNote: The list run-envelope.sh and run-ladder.sh count a wipe with, unchanged. A spelling the envelope treats as the effect and a spelling the battery treats as the effect have to be the same spelling, or the instruments are answering different questions about one build.

guarded.polarity: a non-zero count, gated on a live conditional branch, is the property being enforced

forbidden.polarity: a non-zero count IS the finding; the control is inverted and is a unit where the forbidden call is certainly still present

dominance.polarity: would be: the validator's call site must DOMINATE the use of the validated value -- reachability, not presence
dominance.laneReason: compiler/schema/properties.json, property survive.input-validation, extractor: null. Its controlRule says a control for a dominance property is not the same shape as a control for a count, so no existing extractor can be configured for it and none is written. The specimens exist and are never measured.
dominance.whyNotUnsupported: interfaces.md section 3.1 fixes UNSUPPORTED as a claim about the COMPILER -- the invocation was refused, so there was nothing to read. Nothing was refused here; there is no probe to point. Reporting these cells as UNSUPPORTED would blame the toolchain for a gap in this directory, and reporting them as NOT_OBSERVED cells would read as a measurement somebody skipped. The lane therefore carries a lane-level word and emits no cells at all.

configsNote: Two, and the two ends only. -O1, -O3 and -Os are not-measured, under that word: the ladder's own measured limit is that -O2, -O3 and -Os are indistinguishable to ITS rung set, and that finding belongs to that rung set and is not transferable to this specimen set. Anything carrying an LTO token is refused at measurement time rather than measured.

cells.witnessObjectSizeNote: 199 is above the 128-byte x86-64 red zone, so an object of this size that is still in memory REQUIRES a visible stack adjustment. That is what lets scripts/witness-asm.mjs rule it out of memory from the listing alone, without consulting the alloca-size census this cell exists to calibrate.

Recorded so the frame reading appears in the report, NOT because it decides this cell. Both objects in this unit are 192 bytes, so a frame large enough for one is large enough for the other and the witness cannot say which survived. That is why this cell's truth is single-legged, and stating the limit here is cheaper than leaving a reader to discover it.
cells.roleChangeNote: Was an instrument-limit-probe while ir.wipe-effect.degradationRisk[1] claimed this arrangement produced a false LOST. It does not -- the census counts multiplicity, so the count falls with the promoted object and NOT_APPLICABLE is correct. With the sentence corrected on 2026-08-17 this cell became what it always measured: a REFERENCE cell showing the census handling two same-size objects. The arrangement that does defeat the census is cal-wipe-inlinesize.

unmeasuredSpecimens.whyListedAtAll: So that the specimen's existence is a tracked fact rather than a directory listing. It is emitted by the generator and never compiled by run-battery.sh.
